- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast toward historical mean by 1–3% per period.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–2 periods; adjust forecast 1–2 steps ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (1–5 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “volatility dampener” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 3 days.
